lesson.subject: inquiry
lesson.title: The Business Plan
lesson.subtitle: Shark Tank | Term 4 Week 5, Session 4
lesson.footer: Shark Tank | Grade 5 Inquiry | Week 5 Session 4

plan.curriculum: Victorian Curriculum Economics and Business, Levels 5 and 6: types of resources (natural, human, capital) and how they are used to make what people want; Design and Technologies, Levels 5 and 6: planning the materials and steps to produce a design
plan.shape: 15 minutes explicit, 40 minutes team time: upcycling kids on BTN, the three kinds of resources on Pocket Pal, a quick sorting round, then teams write their business plan
plan.criticalFeature: every product uses natural, human and capital resources; upcycling saves natural resources because the materials already exist
decisionPoints: the Natural, human or capital? round
the choice check: which resource upcycling saves
the exit board: three resources for a new product
plan.anchor: Find a problem. Upcycle a fix. Pitch it.
plan.catchUp: Missed the homeroom sessions? Say: your team found a problem, the Grade 6s tested three ideas, and the market chose one. Your team catches you up in two minutes.

studentTools: Each team's Session 3 Token Test results and final product
manipulatives: A Pocket Pal model, or old jeans, scissors and a sewing needle to hold up during the I Do
The class junk tubs the Grade 5s bring from their homerooms
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: Three headings on the board: Natural, Human, Capital
The team list from the homerooms, with each team's final product
videos: BTN Upcycling Kids (2015, about 4 min): students turn hard-to-recycle waste into pencil cases and bags (abc.net.au/btn/classroom/upcycling-kids/10527044)

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your team's business plan: the product, the problem, the market and every resource you need.
resources.title: Our Business Plan
resources.subtitle: Write every team member's name. Hand this in on Shark Tank Day.

example.prompt: Pocket Pal needs scissors. Natural, human or capital?
steps: Ask: is it from nature, a person, or a tool people made?
Scissors are a tool people made, used again and again.
Tools and machines are capital.

items.prompt: Sort each resource for a team making bird houses from old fence palings.

example.prompt: Fill in the business details for Pocket Pal.
steps: Name: Pocket Pal. Product: a hanging pocket for your bag hook.
Problem: hats and bottles fall off bag hooks.
Target market: kids at school with bag hooks.
example.answer: Pocket Pal | hanging pocket | things fall off hooks | kids with bag hooks

items.prompt: Fill in your team's business details.
answers: e.g. a hat clip made from bread tags and string
e.g. hats get lost at lunch

example.prompt: List one resource Pocket Pal needs and where it comes from.
steps: Resource: denim. It comes from old jeans.
Old jeans are already made, so it is upcycled.
Who brings it? Sam's family has two old pairs.
example.answer: Denim | natural | upcycled from old jeans | Sam

items.prompt: List the resources your team needs. Use at least one of each kind.
Sketch your first design. Label each part with what it is made from.
items.answer: A sketch with labels naming the upcycled material for each part.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option: work out what upcycling saves your team.
resources.title: Extension: What Upcycling Saves
resources.subtitle: Upcycled materials cost less and save natural resources.

sections.title: Count the savings
sections.intro: When you upcycle, you don't pay for new materials. The money you save is the difference between the new price and the upcycled price.

example.prompt: New denim costs $12. Old jeans from home cost $0. How much does upcycling save?
steps: New price: $12.
Upcycled price: $0.

items.prompt: Work out the savings for each material.

example.prompt: Why does a cardboard box made from an old box save a natural resource?
steps: New cardboard is made from trees.
Using an old box means no new cardboard is needed.
Fewer trees are cut down.
example.answer: It saves trees, a natural resource.

items.prompt: Pick one material your team is upcycling. Which natural resource does it save, and how?
items.answer: e.g. Old T-shirts: new cotton needs land and lots of water to grow, so we save cotton and water.

resources.description: Picture clues for the three kinds of resources, and a business plan with sentence starters.

steps: Scissors are a tool.
People made them.

Our product is a hanging pocket.
It fixes hats falling off hooks.

example.answer: Our product is a hanging pocket. It fixes hats falling off hooks. It is made from old jeans.

items.hint: Our product is ___. It fixes ___. It is made from ___.
items.answer: Our product is ___. It fixes ___. It is made from ___.

slides.notes: First Grade 5 Shark Tank session. One line: today every team writes the plan that turns its idea into a real business.

slides.title: For the Shark Tank teachers: Weeks 5 to 10
lines: Two groups of about 30 Grade 5s, each made of whole homeroom classes, one Shark Tank teacher each.
Every session: about 15 minutes taught, 40 minutes of team work, 5 minutes to exit and reflect.
The business plan from this session is the assessment piece, handed in on Monday 7 December.
slides.notes: Teacher-facing overview for Sessions 4 to 8 and Shark Tank Day. Skip it on the board.

Teams seated together from the homeroom class lists. Make one Pocket Pal per Shark Tank teacher before this week, from old jeans; its strap rips in Week 6's demo. Cue the BTN clip. Print the Worksheet one per team, plus a few Extension and Supported copies. Grade 5s bring their class junk tubs from homeroom; sort them by material as they arrive.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning how a business plans the resources it needs.
successCriteria: I can name the three kinds of resources.
I can sort my team's resources into natural, human and capital.
I can complete my team's business plan.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Your team has its product. Today you plan everything it needs.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: Fifteen minutes with me, then forty minutes for your team. Let's be quick.
notes.prep: 15 minutes explicit, 40 team time. SC1 naming resources for all; SC2 sorting is the core; SC3 the plan. Anchor: Find a problem. Upcycle a fix. Pitch it.

slides.title: Kids who turn rubbish into products

notes.answer: toothpaste tubes and other hard-to-recycle waste, made into bows, pencil cases and bags
beats: PLAY the whole BTN story from the link, about 4 minutes.
SAY: Watch what these kids start with, and what they end up with.
ASK: What did they start with, and what did they make?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: toothpaste tubes, made into pencil cases and bags
SCAN for both parts: the waste and the product.
80%+ -> cold call one pair: why upcycle, not bin it?
Less -> replay the first minute, re-ask.
ASK: Thumbs: could you upcycle something from your bin at home?
5 sec. Cue: thumbs at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: thumbs up
trap: Fix: ask whether the tube was broken down or kept and changed, student says upcycled.
notes.prep: Launch. The BTN story shows waste as a resource. About 6 minutes including the clip discussion.

slides.label: Turn and tell: what did they start with, and what did they make?

slides.meaning: Everything a business uses to make its product: natural, human and capital.
slides.example: Pocket Pal's resources are old jeans, the team's sewing, and a pair of scissors.

notes.answer: everything a business uses to make its product
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Resources. Say it with me. Re-sour-ces.
SAY: Natural resources come from nature. Human resources are people's work.
Capital is the tools and machines people made.
ASK: Scissors. Natural, human or capital?
10 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: capital
ASK: Name one natural resource in this room.
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: wood, paper, water
trap: Fix: in business, capital also means tools and machines. Student names one.
notes.prep: One key word carrying three kinds. Point to the three board headings as you say each.

slides.title: Pocket Pal's resources
slides.label: Upcycling: the jeans already exist, so no new cotton is grown.

notes.answer: natural: cotton, water; human: designer, sewer, seller; capital: scissors, needle, glue gun
beats: HOLD UP the old jeans.
ASK: Cotton grown on a farm. Natural, human or capital?
5 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: natural
POINT to the Human column.
ASK: The person who sews it. Which column?
5 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: human
ASK: Scissors and a needle. Which column?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: capital
SAY: And because the jeans already exist, no new cotton is grown. That's upcycling.
trap: putting the old jeans under capital because they were made by people.
Fix: ask what jeans are made of, student says cotton, natural.
notes.stretch: Why is the sewing machine capital but the thread natural?
notes.help: Point to each column and say one example aloud with the student.
notes.prep: The model for SC2. Pocket Pal is the class model business; keep the jeans on the desk all term.

slides.title: Natural, human or capital?
slides.pivot: ask: from nature, a person, or a tool? then re-ask
slides.followUp: cold call one board: how do you know?

items.text: The person who presents the pitch

items.answer: Natural - cardboard is made from trees

say: Quick round. Write N, H or C
trap: calling cardboard or wool capital because a factory made it.
Fix: ask what it is made of, student traces it back to nature.
notes.stretch: Name a resource that could be two kinds, and say why.
notes.help: Keep the three board headings with one picture each.
notes.prep: First decision point: sorting new resources. Brisk: one line of feedback per item. SC2. Five items, about 4 minutes.

slides.title: What does upcycling save?
slides.prompt: Pick the resource upcycling saves most. Point to A, B or C.

options.text: Natural resources, like trees and cotton
Human resources, like the team's work
Capital, like scissors and glue guns

beats: SAY: Think about what we don't need to grow or cut down.
ASK: What does upcycling save most?
15 sec. Cue: voices off. Point... now.
EXPECT: A
SCAN pointing fingers, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one A: why not B?
Less -> hold up the jeans: was new cotton grown? re-ask.
REVEAL after fingers are scanned.
SAY: Natural resources. The materials already exist. Tick or fix.
trap: choosing B because upcycling feels easier.
Fix: ask whether the team still has to build it, student re-chooses.
notes.prep: Second decision point and the reason the sharks invest in upcycling. Under 80% means repeat the jeans example before team time.

slides.title: Write your business plan
slides.task: With your team: fill in your business details, list every resource and who brings it, then sketch your first design.
slides.extendedTask: a team business plan: business details, a resources list with who brings what, and a labelled first design

notes.answer: a plan with natural, human and capital resources, and who brings each
beats: SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Everyone, together, on three: Natural. Human. Capital.
TIME 40 minutes. At 20, stop for a check.
ASK: Thumbs: does every resource have a name beside it?
5 sec. Cue: thumbs at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: thumbs up
CIRCULATE. Ask: what's upcycled? Who's bringing it? What if they forget?
TIME at 40: each team names one thing it still needs from home.
trap: a resources list with nothing upcycled.
Fix: team swaps one new material for something from the junk tubs.
notes.stretch: Extension: work out what upcycling saves in money and natural resources.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture clues and sentence starters. Sit with the team for the first row.
notes.prep: The business plan is assessment evidence, handed in on Shark Tank Day. Building starts next week, so materials lists must be done today.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: A team makes book stands from old cereal boxes, cut with scissors by Ava.
Name one natural, one human and one capital resource.

notes.answer: natural: the cardboard; human: Ava's cutting; capital: the scissors
beats: SAY: A new product. Work on your own.
ASK: Name one natural, one human and one capital resource.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: cardboard, Ava, scissors
RECORD who swaps capital and natural.
trap: writing the book stand as the capital.
Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new product. One board per student.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner one thing you must bring from home for next week's build.
slides.selfAssessment: Fist to five: how ready is your team to start building?

notes.answer: a named material and who is bringing it
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: Fist to five: how ready is your team to start building?
5 sec. Cue: fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: mostly three to five
RECORD teams showing fists and ones. Check their materials list first next week.
ASK: Tell your partner what you must bring from home.
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: a material and who brings it
notes.prep: Next week is build day one. Teams without materials use the junk tubs. SC3.
